tax_litigation.status: A show cause notice dated September 25 (“SCN”) was issued to our company by Deputy Commissioner of State Tax, Mumbai (“DCST”), for an aggregate amount of Rs.140.53 million, alleging contravention in relation to credit notes, and tax liabilities arising from excess input credit claimed by our Company, corporate guarantees and bank guarantees issued by our Company, amongst others, from April 2021 to March 2022. Subsequently, pursuant to the replies submitted by our Company and order dated December 2, 2025 issued by the DCST, the aggregate amount was modified and reduced to Rs. 97.69 million. Our Company filed an appeal dated March 2, 2026 before the first appellate authority. The matter is currently pending.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: An adjudication order dated February 12, 2025 (“Adjudication Order”) was issued to our Company by the Office of the State Tax Officer, Department of Goods and Services Tax, Government of Maharashtra, for an aggregate amount of ₹52.91 million. The order alleges (i) excess claim of input tax credit, (ii) failure to discharge tax liability on corporate guarantees extended by the Company to its subsidiaries, and (iii) interest on delayed payment of tax for the period from April 2020 to March 2021. Our company filed an appeal dated May 6, 2025 (“Appeal”) before the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax (Appeal), seeking to quash the Adjudication Order. The matter is currently pending.
tax_litigation.status: An adjudication order dated February 12, 2025 (“Adjudication Order”) was issued to our Company by the Office of the State Tax Officer, Department of Goods and Services Tax, Government of Maharashtra, for an aggregate amount of ₹52.91 million. The order alleges (i) excess claim of input tax credit, (ii) failure to discharge tax liability on corporate guarantees extended by the Company to its subsidiaries, and (iii) interest on delayed payment of tax for the period from April 2020 to March 2021. Our company filed an appeal dated May 6, 2025 (“Appeal”) before the Deputy Commissioner of State Tax (Appeal), seeking to quash the Adjudication Order. Our company has received the personal hearing notice on March 24, 2026. The personal hearing is scheduled on April 8,2026. The matter is currently pending.

FY - 2022-23 A draft order under section 144C(1) of the Income Tax Act has been received dated 18 March 2026 wherein certain additions has been proposed. In this regard, we shall file an appeal before CIT(A) once we receive a final order under section 143(3) of the Act.

tax_litigation.status: FY - 2022-23 A final assessment order under section 143(3) read with section 144C(3) read with section 144B of the Income-tax Act, 1961 ('the Act') was passed dated 23 April 2026 wherein certain additions has been made to returned income in case of Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Limited (Formerly known as Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Private Limited) ('CMES') In this regard, we have filed an appeal before CIT(A) dated 22 May 2026.

FY - 2021-22 With respect to the litigation of Surya Energy Photovoltaic India Private Limited ('Surya'), a subsidiary of CMES, submissions were made before the AO requesting for a complete stay of demand amounting to INR 65,44,53,680 till disposal of the appeal before the CIT(A). Pursuant to which stay on collection of the entire demand were granted through multiple orders. A stay order dated 20 April 2026 was granted till 30 June 2026. Subsequently, an application for extension for stay of demand was filed on 30 June 2026.

Targeting to commission atleast ~1 GW of STU Connected projects across 7 states in India and rooftop projects across multiple sites simultaneously in FY 2026-27.

operating_notes.text: Clean Max has 5.7 GW of operational and contracted renewable capacity across India, the Middle East, and South-East Asia as of March 2026

Clean Max Solomon Private Limited (CIN U35105MH2025PTC446454) was incorporated on 23 April 2025 and Clean Max Ilgohp Private Limited (CIN U35105MH2025PTC459619) on 24 October 2025; neither contributed turnover, revenue, income or net worth
Clean Max Taurus Private Limited is a 51:49 JV between Clean Max and Apple India for 51 MWp solar projects.

Corporate guarantees approved for 13 subsidiaries' term loans, including ₹87 Cr for Clean Max Louise, ₹41.45 Cr for Clean Max Gaia and ₹29 Cr for Clean Max Hydra; described as contingent liabilities with no impact on the company as on date.
Q4FY26 power-sales segment EBITDA was ₹338.46 Cr on revenue of ₹369.37 Cr; services segment EBITDA was ₹29.87 Cr on revenue of ₹185.19 Cr.
IPO fresh issue of ₹1,202.98 Cr (net ₹1,149.25 Cr) was used to prepay ₹523.67 Cr of borrowings by 31 March 2026, with ₹599 Cr more prepaid on 2 April 2026.
The group had 161 subsidiaries and 7 step-down subsidiaries plus 3 joint ventures at 31 March 2026.
FY26 weighted average realised tariff was ₹4.20/kWh, down from ₹4.28/kWh in FY25.
Contracted capacity of 5,685 MW includes 2,597 MW yet to be executed; 69% solar and 31% wind.
Data & AI customers account for 42% of contracted capacity as of 31 March 2026.
Clean Max operational RE power sales capacity reached 3,088 MW as of March 31, 2026.
Data and AI customers account for 42% of contracted capacity as of April 2026.
Secured ~$575 million through multi-lender facilities for ~1 GW renewable projects across Rajasthan and Karnataka.
Clean Max Celestial Private Limited commissioned 351.4 MWp in Bikaner Solar Park.
Parent support of ₹108 Cr (Clean Max Emerald) and ₹61 Cr (Clean Max Teton) given as security for term loans from Aseem Infrastructure Finance Limited, booked as contingent liability.
Clean Max partnered with GACL for 75.90 MW wind and 84.34 MWp solar hybrid project in Gujarat.
Board approved issuance of listed secured NCDs up to ₹2,500 Cr on private placement basis for capex and debt refinancing.
Board approved scheme of amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiaries Clean Max Aditya Power, Cleanmax IPP 1, CMES Power 1, and CMES Infinity into the parent.
The group is consolidating its rooftop business segment into a single entity to manage projects as one integrated portfolio.
Operational capacity reached 3,493 MW as of June 30, 2026, with total contracted capacity at 6,831 MW.
Operational capacity reached 3.5 GW as of June 30, 2026, with total contracted capacity at 6 GW.
Issued a corporate guarantee not exceeding ₹92 Cr for subsidiary Clean Max Rudra Private Limited in favour of Federal Bank Limited.
Received BSE in-principle approval to modify terms of 40,000 NCDs worth up to ₹400 Cr from unsecured to secured with a 1:1 security cover.
Approved a term sheet with Envision Energy India Private Limited for procuring 1,550 MW of wind turbine generators across 310 units in seven phases ending by 31 December 2028.
Crisil assigned AA/Stable ratings to ₹2,500 Cr NCDs and corporate credit rating on September 7, 2026.
Appointed Mr. Vipin Balan as Head - Projects.
Approved sale of 26% stakes in Clean Max Kyuu, Clean Max Roku, and Clean Max Ilgohp for ₹26,000 each.
Allotted ₹2,500 Cr green NCDs across five series (Series A to E) with tenors up to 10 years.
Raised ₹2,500 crore through green debt securities (NCDs) across five series with maturities ranging from 2 to 10 years and coupons from 8.25% to 8.76%.
Shareholders approved material related party transactions with 32 subsidiary and fellow subsidiary entities via postal ballot.
CleanMax partnered with Nuvoco on a 46.4 MW wind-solar hybrid project in Rajasthan to supply ~100 MU annually.
Received final BSE approval for modification of 40,000 NCDs from unsecured to secured terms.
Risk Management Committee approved a corporate guarantee not exceeding ₹45.09 crore for subsidiary Clean Max Patagonia Private Limited.
Massmunch Company Limited, incorporated in Thailand on 27 March 2025, had nil turnover at 31 December 2025 and net worth of Thai Baht 1,213,300.

timeline.summary: Clean Max wins 30 MW hybrid renewable energy project from Shell
2026-04-28: Clean Max announced receipt of an income tax assessment order for AY 2023-24 with a demand of ₹6.78 crore.

2026-04-28: Clean Max board approved sale of 4,900 shares of Clean Max Solomon to SAMHI Hotels for ₹49,000 and 2,600 shares of Clean Max Ilgohp to Nuvoco Vistas for ₹26,000, with agreements due by 30 June 2026.
CleanMax and Apple entered into a strategic co-investment partnership of ~₹100 crore to boost renewable energy in India.
Clean Max completed the acquisition of 2,38,732 equity shares in its subsidiary Clean Max Taurus on 7 May 2026.
2026-05-08: Clean Max's Risk Management Committee approved corporate guarantees for term loans of 13 subsidiaries, the largest ₹87 Cr for Clean Max Louise.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹557.46 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹55.42 Cr.
Clean Max issued its FY2026 shareholders' letter reporting 3,088 MW of operational RE power sales capacity and ₹1,870 crore run-rate EBITDA.
Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions Limited’s earnings conference call recording for Q4FY26 and FY26, held on 13 May 2026, is available at the company’s website.
Clean Max disclosed a ₹128 Cr corporate guarantee issued for Clean Max Taurus following changes in subsidiary status.
2026-05-18: Clean Max released its Q4 and FY26 earnings conference call transcript reporting 3,100 MW operational RE capacity and ₹1,295 Cr EBITDA.
On May 19, 2026, Clean Max disclosed the voting results of its postal ballot showing all 48 resolutions passed with requisite majority.
Clean Max received a credit rating upgrade to CARE AA-/Stable from CARE Ratings Limited on May 20, 2026.
On May 26, 2026, Clean Max announced securing ~$575 million through multi-lender transactions for ~1 GW renewable projects across Rajasthan and Karnataka.
Clean Max announced that its wholly owned subsidiary Clean Max Celestial Private Limited commissioned 351.4 MWp of solar capacity in Bikaner Solar Park.

2026-05-27: Clean Max's Risk Management Committee approved hypothecation, pledge and other support for ₹108 Cr and ₹61 Cr term loan facilities of subsidiaries Clean Max Emerald and Clean Max Teton from Aseem Infrastructure Finance Limited.
2026-06-03: Clean Max partnered with Gujarat Alkalies and Chemicals Limited for a 160.24 MW hybrid renewable energy project under a group captive structure.
On July 24, 2026, Clean Max approved selling 26% stakes in Clean Max Sau and Clean Max Ni, and acquiring the remaining 26% stake in Clean Max Uno to make it a wholly owned subsidiary.
Clean Max submitted the scrutinizer's report and voting results for its 16th AGM held on July 24, 2026.
Q1FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹832.16 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹48.52 Cr.
The Board approved a scheme to merge four wholly owned rooftop solar subsidiaries into the parent company to streamline operations.
Clean Max released its Q1 FY27 shareholders' letter reporting 3,493 MW operational capacity, ₹462.9 Cr reported EBITDA, and guiding for a minimum ₹3,000 Cr EBITDA in FY27-28.
Clean Max reported Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹832.16 Cr and PAT of ₹55 Cr, while guiding for a minimum EBITDA of ₹3,000 Cr in FY28.
Clean Max approved a ₹92 Cr corporate guarantee for subsidiary Clean Max Rudra in August 2026.
Clean Max received BSE in-principle approval to modify ₹400 Cr of NCDs from unsecured to secured with a 1:1 security cover.
Clean Max issued a postal ballot notice seeking shareholder approval for 32 material related party transactions aggregating up to several thousand crores across its subsidiaries.
Clean Max approved a term sheet with Envision Energy to procure 1,550 MW of wind turbines across 310 units to be executed in seven phases by December 2028.
Clean Max received Crisil AA/Stable ratings for ₹2,500 Cr NCDs and its corporate credit rating.
Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions approved the sale of its 49% stake in subsidiary Clean Max Dynamis to Sunvik Steels for ₹49,000.
Clean Max approved the sale of 26% stakes in subsidiaries Clean Max Kyuu, Clean Max Roku, and Clean Max Ilgohp, and appointed Vipin Balan as Head - Projects.
Clean Max allotted ₹2,500 Cr of green non-convertible debentures across five series on September 28, 2026.
CleanMax raised ₹2,500 crore through India's first C&I green bond issuance structured across five series.
Clean Max obtained shareholder approval via postal ballot for material related party transactions across 32 subsidiary and group entities on 24 September 2026.
CleanMax partnered with Nuvoco Vistas for a 46.4 MW wind-solar hybrid renewable energy project in Bhikamkhore, Rajasthan.
Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions received BSE listing approval on September 29, 2026, for ₹2,500 crore of green debt securities issued across five series.
Clean Max received final BSE approval on September 30, 2026, to modify 40,000 NCDs from unsecured to secured status.
Clean Max Enviro Energy Solutions approved a corporate guarantee of ₹45.09 crore for its subsidiary Clean Max Patagonia Private Limited.

Clean Max's Thai step-down subsidiaries signed a share purchase agreement on 9 October 2026 to buy 100% of Massmunch Company Limited, a Thai renewable-energy company with nil turnover, for an enterprise value of Thai Baht 1,250,000, with completion indicated for 31 October 2026.
